I didn't run any code; I found this by reading the weights.

**Where it is:** Hidden units 32–35 (the last four rows of W1) are the only units that don't look trained, for two reasons:

1. **They have no effect on play.** Their columns in W2 are all ±0.0, so whatever these units compute never reaches the move scores.
2. **Their input weights look made up.** The W1 rows are small values between 0.08 and 0.25 whose signs simply alternate. Every other row has the uneven mix of sizes you get from training.

Because these units do nothing, their parameters are free to carry a message. Their biases in b1 are the only values that differ meaningfully from one unit to the next:

| Hidden unit | b1 | Value × −100 | ASCII letter |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | −0.82 | 82 | R |
| 33 | −0.73 | 73 | I |
| 34 | −0.83 | 83 | S |
| 35 | −0.65 | 65 | A |

All four values land in the A–Z range of ASCII codes (65–90) and read RISA in unit order.

CODE: RISA
